Thanks — looking for something concise we can share with our procurement team.

Hi Emma — thanks for the context, this is helpful. Below is a concise snapshot of our hosted IO pricing and an inventory of commonly requested models. I’ve also attached a short preview of our baseline ratecard for procurement.

Per-1M token IO pricing (standard hosted tier, USD) — input/output prices listed separately:
- Redwood-3 (large conversational): input $0.40 / 1M, output $0.80 / 1M
- Redwood-XL (high-cap, longer context): input $0.90 / 1M, output $1.80 / 1M
- Open-equivalent (community): input $0.30 / 1M, output $0.60 / 1M
- Fast-small (low-latency): input $0.18 / 1M, output $0.36 / 1M

Notes:
- IO-split matters for cost — summarize-heavy workloads (long outputs) will drive the output side.
- Long-context variants (>=8k tokens) carry a per-token premium (~2x) due to memory/KV costs; listed under Redwood-XL.
- Embeddings and reranking are priced separately — happy to send that if you need it.

Volume & introductory discounts (examples):
- Intro credit: $5k credit for new accounts that convert within 30 days of pilot (one-off).
- Committed discount tiers (monthly committed spend): 10% @ 20M tokens/mo, 20% @ 50M tokens/mo, 30% @ 150M tokens/mo — final terms depend on contract length and SLA tier.

Latency guidance (short prompts, <512 tokens): typical median latency with our hosted small/fast models ~80–150ms; with Redwood-3 ~180–260ms depending on region and concurrency. Long-context responses vary and often exceed 300ms.

Attachments: Redwood-Hosted-Baseline-Ratecard-Preview.pdf (attached) — includes the same numbers plus example IO-cost math for typical prompt sizes.

If you’d like, I can:
- Send a simple cost worksheet if you share expected prompt lengths and output sizes.
- Propose a committed discount schedule and term sheet for procurement.
- Book a 30-min call to walk through latency/cost tradeoffs — calendly link: https://calendly.com/jonas-weber/redwood-intro-30m

Would you prefer a short call or a worksheet first?

Thanks,

Hi Emma, answers inline below.

1) Committed discounts: yes — discounts apply to the total charged IO (input + output) according to the contracted tier. We compute baseline cost as (input_tokens * input_rate) + (output_tokens * output_rate) and then apply the committed discount percentage.

2) Long-context premium: two options — (A) automatic per-token premium if you call the long-context variant (we host specific long-context model variants), or (B) use our short-context model with pinned rolling KV cache (not all customers do this). For clarity: if you select Redwood-XL (>=8k), you’ll be billed at the long-context rate.

3) Intro credit: the $5k credit is applied after account verification and a first paid invoice — effectively a one-time rebate on initial spend; we can discuss a different pilot credit structure for procurement-driven pilots.

Example math (to illustrate how IO and discount interact):
- Pilot: 10M tokens/mo, mix 60% input / 40% output, using Redwood-3
  - Input cost: 6M * $0.40 = $2.40
  - Output cost: 4M * $0.80 = $3.20
  - Monthly total = $5.60 (per 1M-token basis) * 10 = $56 (this is illustrative; see attached sheet for per-month math)

If you ramp to 50M and qualify for 20% commit, same math scales and we apply 20% off the computed monthly bill.

Next steps:
- If you can share a usage snapshot I’ll drop a one-page cost worksheet.
- Otherwise, pick a 30-min slot on my calendar and we’ll map out model selection and SLOs.

Looping in Lauren (cc) who manages procurement for pilot commercial terms.

Cheers,
Jonas
